newsitem.title: GREECE: FOREIGN BLUE CHIP BUYING LIFTS GREEK STOCKS AT OPEN.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN BLUE CHIP BUYING LIFTS GREEK STOCKS AT OPEN.

text.p: Greek equities kicked off the week
on a firm note on continuing strength in blue chip banks,
industrials and OTE telecom which brokers attributed
to dollar-linked buying interest from abroad.
"We have seen increased foreign buying in the past few
sessions in core institutional holdings which are the result of
a stronger dollar," said Alexis Panagiotopoulos, broker at
InterSec.
"But the market continues to operate below its capacity due
to the summer holiday doldrums, even though it does offer
trading opportunities in number of blue chips," he added.
The dollar's rise in international markets, however, was
also seen as a potential source of friction in Greece's efforts
to converge with other European Union economies.
"The market is still undecided about the medium- and
long-term effects of the rise in the dollar/drachma rate on the
Greek economy and will keep a warry eye on forthcoming
macroeconomic announcements," said Panagiotopoulos.
The Athens benchmark index was 0.37 percent or 6.12 points
firmer at 1,645.56 from Friday's 1,639.44 after 25 minutes of
trading.
Banks and industrials were up 0.30 and 0.41 percent
respectively.
Other sectors were also moving along with the trend in large
caps.
Turnover was 1.7 billion drachmas on volume of 0.4 million
shares.
Advancers were leading decliners 87 to 33 with 22 shares
unchanged on 142 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were
quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.6-$11.0. Two
GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike
price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at
1,124-1,154 drachmas.
The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread
warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at
10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,094-1,154 drachmas. The
warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying
stock were up 85 drachmas at 6,530.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23
Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was
quoted at 685.12-728.85 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9
The ING Baring Financial Products American style call
warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at
$76.40-$79.24. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the
warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call
warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas
was quoted at 3,846-4,075 drachmas. The strike price is set at
10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a
basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.60 bid/no offer. The
strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9
The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma-
denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was
quoted at 250-283 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639
points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
